capitals.name: Nidaros (Trondheim)
capitals.note: Bridging entry for Magnus's seat, which neither Magnus page names (M1 has him dying in Denmark and 'buried with his father in the cathedral at Nidaros, modern Trondheim'). Trondheim page, opened in the repair pass: 'The settlement was founded in 997 as a trading post and served as the capital of Norway through the Viking Age until 1217.' So Nidaros is the Norwegian capital of the years 1042-1047 by the page, but not the seat of the union as such: confidence of a bridging entry.

rulers.name: Magnus the Good
rulers.note: King of Norway from 1035, king of Denmark from 1042; died 25 October 1047.

correction.text: Magnus's two kingdoms, Norway and Denmark with Scania, as Cliopatria draws them in 1046

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1042-1045, years Cliopatria draws otherwise: Norway in its own row and Denmark inside the Denmark-England shape (wrong after June 1042). M1: 'In 1042, he was also crowned king of Denmark.' In 1043 Sweyn returned with the Wends and Magnus beat them at Lyrskov Heath near Hedeby. Repair pass: the first version drew Denmark as the modern country ({country Denmark}, 50,327 km2) and so left out Scania, Halland, Blekinge and southern Schleswig, which both neighbouring Cliopatria shapes (Denmark-England 1040 and this row's 1046) hold (56, 26 and 13 cells of Skåne, Halland and Blekinge; the corrected spec holds all three, checked with the gazetteer). The Danish kingdom Magnus was crowned over included Scania: M1 has Sweyn press Magnus 'from his base in Scania' (a claimant's base inside the realm, not a Swedish province). The 1046 outline is the sum of the Norwegian (296.3 k km2) and Danish (82.6 k km2) parts in Cliopatria and is used unchanged for 1042-1045.

379,163 km2, -7.60E..19.38E, 54.07N..69.79N: Norway and Denmark together, and the sum of Cliopatria's Norwegian (296.3 k) and Danish (82.6 k) shapes. Valid as a union only to Magnus's death on 25 October 1047: M1 'On 25 October 1047, Magnus suddenly died while in Denmark' and 'his kingdom was split between Harald Hardrada in Norway and Sweyn Estridsson in Denmark'. For 1048-1055 the same lands are two kingdoms, Norway under Harald and Denmark under Sweyn, drawn by the Old Kingdom of Norway and Kingdom of Denmark dossiers; Cliopatria has neither row in those years. The row's Wikipedia page and Wikidata id (Q62651) belong to the later Denmark-Norway union (D1: 'Dual monarchy (Real union) (1537-1814)') and say nothing of Magnus.

correction.text: unchanged shape; the years should read 1046..1047 as one realm (Magnus died 25 October 1047); from 1048 the Norwegian part belongs to Harald Hardrada and the Danish part to Sweyn Estridsson

region.text: Norway, Magnus's since 1035, and Denmark with Scania, crowned in 1042 (Cliopatria's 1046 outline of the two kingdoms)

ledger.note: 1042: Magnus the Good of Norway is crowned king of Denmark as well. M1: 'In 1042, he was also crowned king of Denmark.' after 'In 1042, Harthacnut died while in England.' Sweyn Estridsson also claimed the throne.

region.text: Denmark, claimed by Sweyn Estridsson; the Wend invasion of 1043 at Lyrskov Heath near Hedeby

ledger.note: 1043: Sweyn Estridsson returns with the Wends and Magnus defeats them at Lyrskov Heath. M1: 'Sweyn fled east and returned as one of the leaders of an invasion by the Wends in 1043.' The battle was near Hedeby: 'It was the greatest victory ever over the Wends, with up to 15,000 killed.' Zone read as Denmark, the crown Sweyn claimed.
Late 1046: Sweyn is driven out of Denmark. M1: 'by late 1046, Magnus had driven Sweyn out of Denmark'; in 1046 Magnus also made Harald Hardrada his co-king in Norway.

region.text: Norway, to Harald Hardrada, and Denmark, to Sweyn Estridsson

ledger.note: 25 October 1047: Magnus dies and his two kingdoms part. M1: 'On 25 October 1047, Magnus suddenly died while in Denmark.' 'After his death, his kingdom was split between Harald Hardrada in Norway and Sweyn Estridsson in Denmark.'

wars.name: Magnus the Good against Sweyn Estridsson and the Wends

zones.text: Denmark, with Hedeby and Lyrskov Heath

wars.outcome: Magnus won at Lyrskov Heath in 1043 and had driven Sweyn out of Denmark by late 1046; after Magnus died in October 1047 Denmark went to Sweyn.
wars.note: M1 does not date Sweyn's election as king at Viborg or the Battle of Helganes, which other sources place in these years.

certainty.note: Two kingdoms under one king; their coasts and inland frontiers are unsurveyed, and the Wend and Swedish frontiers are approximate.

notes:
DECISION: Norway-Denmark is Magnus the Good's union of the two kingdoms, 1042 to his death on 25 October 1047 (Cliopatria 1046-1055). It is a different state from Denmark-Norway (1537-1814), although Cliopatria gives both the Wikipedia title 'Denmark-Norway' and Wikidata Q62651: D1 dates the later union 1537-1814 and says nothing about the 1040s. The two rows must not be merged; denmark-norway belongs to eu-14 (another part) and should have its own wikidata/title note.
CLIOPATRIA YEARS: the row starts 1046 and runs to 1055, but the union began in 1042 (new keyframe 1042-1045; those years are drawn by the old-kingdom-of-norway row for Norway and wrongly by the denmark-england shape for Denmark) and ended in October 1047. For 1048-1055 Norway (Harald Hardrada) and Denmark (Sweyn Estridsson) are separate kingdoms that Cliopatria draws as one shape, because it has no Old Kingdom of Norway shape 1046-1055 and no Kingdom of Denmark shape 1018-1055; the kingdom-of-denmark and old-kingdom-of-norway dossiers should supply 1048-1055 or the renderer should keep this shape for those years in two colours.
NOT ON THE PAGES: Sweyn's election at Viborg, the Battle of Helganes (1044 in other sources), Magnus's claim on England in 1045 (M1 has only a letter to Edward after 1042), any area or capital. The capital is a bridging entry.
NORWAY DRAWN TWICE (open): this dossier draws Norway and Denmark together for 1042-1047, as Cliopatria draws a union row over its parts (the Kalmar Union precedent), but the old-kingdom-of-norway dossier (eu-14-c, repaired) also draws Norway: its keyframe _1040 runs on to 1045 and its new keyframe _1046 covers 1046-1055. The two overlap on Norway in 1042-1047; from 1048 only the Norway dossier draws it, and nobody draws Denmark (no kingdom-of-denmark dossier yet; Cliopatria has no Danish row 1018-1055). Either old-kingdom-of-norway pauses (merge 1042, split 1047) or this dossier's corrections drop the Norwegian half (minus the Old Kingdom of Norway shape); this dossier leaves that to the reviewer. Pages used: 2 of 2.
REPAIR PASS 2026-10-25 (reviewer's finding): the 1042-1045 keyframe and the 1042 'found' region drew Denmark as the modern country, which leaves out Scania, Halland, Blekinge and southern Schleswig that Cliopatria's neighbouring shapes hold; both now use Cliopatria's own Norway-Denmark outline of 1046. The Magnus the Good page (reopened) names Scania only as Sweyn's base and does not name Halland, Blekinge or Schleswig, so the extent of Magnus's Denmark rests on Cliopatria's outline and the page's 'crowned king of Denmark'. The capital now cites the Trondheim page (Nidaros capital of Norway to 1217) and stays a bridging entry. Still open for the orchestrator: Norway is drawn twice in 1042-1047 (this dossier and old-kingdom-of-norway), see the paragraph above.
